content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To remove e6000 glue, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Identify the material surface type (5 minutes)
Step 2. Put on heavy-duty nitrile gloves (1 minute)
Step 3. Dispose of used scraping tools (2 minutes)
Step 4. Apply a final layer of surface polish (10 minutes)
Step 5. Test a small amount of acetone on an inconspicuous area (10 minutes)
Step 6. Lay down a protective drop cloth (5 minutes)
Step 7. Gently pry the edge of the glue with a putty knife (5 minutes)
Step 8. Use a hair dryer to soften the bond (8 minutes)
Step 9. Apply a citrus-based adhesive remover (15 minutes)
Step 10. Buff the area with a microfiber cloth (5 minutes)
Step 11. Scrape away the primary softened mass (12 minutes)
Step 12. Soak a cotton ball in nail polish remover (2 minutes)
Step 13. Agitate the residue with a stiff-bristled brush (6 minutes)
Step 14. Gather all necessary chemical solvents (10 minutes)
Step 15. Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly to stubborn spots (20 minutes)
Step 16. Ventilate the room by opening windows (5 minutes)
Step 17. Wipe away dissolved glue with a paper towel (3 minutes)
Step 18. Use a plastic razor blade for fine detailing (10 minutes)
Step 19. Pour a small amount of naphtha onto the residue (5 minutes)
Step 20. Prepare a warm soapy water solution (4 minutes)
Step 21. Use a pumice stone for textured surfaces (7 minutes)
Step 22. Inspect the surrounding area for drips (2 minutes)
Step 23. Rub the area with 70% isopropyl alcohol (5 minutes)
Step 24. Clean the surface with a degreaser (6 minutes)
Step 25. Apply a silicone-based lubricant to loosen edges (10 minutes)
Step 26. Rinse the area with clear water (3 minutes)
Step 27. Locate a heat gun for industrial-strength bonds (5 minutes)
Step 28. Apply a commercial glue-gone solution (12 minutes)
Step 29. Use a fine-grit sandpaper for mechanical removal (15 minutes)
Step 30. Check the MSDS for safety precautions (10 minutes)
Step 31. Wipe down the workbench (5 minutes)
Step 32. Use a steel wool pad for metal surfaces (8 minutes)
Step 33. Apply a specialized lacquer thinner (10 minutes)
Step 34. Let the solvent sit for deep penetration (30 minutes)
Step 35. Perform a final visual inspection (2 minutes)
Step 36. Secure the workpiece in a vice (4 minutes)
Step 37. Use a dental pick for crevices (15 minutes)
Step 38. Saturate a rag with white spirit (10 minutes)
Step 39. Apply a heat-conductive gel (5 minutes)
Step 40. Buy a fresh bottle of acetone (30 minutes)
Step 41. Research specific solvent compatibility (20 minutes)
Step 42. Wipe the surface with a tack cloth (2 minutes)
Step 43. Clean and store the chemical containers (10 minutes)
Step 44. Re-apply solvent to dry patches (5 minutes)
Step 45. Scrape the remaining film with a fingernail (4 minutes)
Step 46. Dab the spot with a vinegar-soaked cloth (8 minutes)
Step 47. Seal the waste bag (2 minutes)
Step 48. Use an old toothbrush for scrubbing (5 minutes)
Step 49. Apply a penetrating oil (15 minutes)
Step 50. Dry the surface with a lint-free towel (3 minutes)
Step 51. Apply a specialized adhesive emulsifier (12 minutes)
Step 52. Check the expiration date on the solvent (1 minute)
Step 53. Wash your hands thoroughly (3 minutes)
Step 54. Put on a respirator mask (2 minutes)
Step 55. Clear the workspace of clutter (10 minutes)
Step 56. Apply a baking soda paste (15 minutes)
Step 57. Scrub the area with a nylon pad (7 minutes)
Step 58. Read the glue manufacturer's removal guide (10 minutes)
Step 59. Apply a layer of masking tape around the spot (5 minutes)
Step 60. Use a flathead screwdriver for prying (4 minutes)
Step 61. Label the waste containers (5 minutes)
Step 62. Set up a portable fan for airflow (3 minutes)
Step 63. Take a photo of the progress (1 minute)
Step 64. Use a copper wool pad for non-scratching (10 minutes)
Step 65. Organize the removal tools on a tray (5 minutes)
Step 66. Sharpen the scraper blade (6 minutes)
Step 67. Fetch a bucket of water (4 minutes)
Step 68. Vacuum up any dried glue flakes (5 minutes)
Step 69. Apply a final rinse of denatured alcohol (4 minutes)
Step 70. Use a steam cleaner for heat-based loosening (12 minutes)
